chunks: With the first chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from a man, from one of them both (peace be upon them), regarding the meaning of His saying, Glorified and Mighty: "Thus Allah will show them their deeds as anguish for them" [2:167].

He said: It is the man who earns wealth but is deprived of doing good with it, and then he dies. Another inherits it and does righteous deeds with it. So the first man sees what he earned appearing as good deeds in the scale of another.

key_terms.ميزان: The Scale -- of deeds on Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of Quran 2:167 about showing deeds as regrets?
ai.summary: An unnamed Imam (either al-Baqir or al-Sadiq) interprets Quran 2:167 as referring to one who accumulates wealth but fails to spend it charitably. Upon death, his heir uses the same wealth for righteous deeds. The original earner then witnesses his own efforts yielding rewards in another person's balance on the Day of Judgment -- a source of anguish and regret.
